source_resources.author: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan N. Gomez, Łukasz Kaiser, Illia Polosukhin
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 3.2.1: Scaled Dot-Product Attention equation and query/key/value matrix definitions
source_resources.license: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license / Open Access
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference to open-access paper; all explanations and mathematical formulations in this curriculum are original works.
source_resources.prerequisites: Linear algebra, matrix multiplication, softmax probability distributions
source_resources.selection_rationale: The foundational primary literature establishing scaled dot-product attention, multi-head projection mechanisms, and autoregressive causal masking.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Open-access paper freely hosted on arXiv.org; no paywall.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Complete original algebraic derivations, matrix examples, variance proofs, and tensor diagrams are self-contained in the curriculum text without external document dependency.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Bahdanau et al.: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate (ICLR 2015)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Pioneered additive attention in RNNs, but Vaswani scaled dot-product attention replaced additive alignment in modern LLM architectures due to parallel matrix multiplication speed.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Shaw et al.: Self-Attention with Relative Position Representations (NAACL 2018)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Introduces relative positional biases into attention; deferred to subsequent positional embedding modules after absolute scaled attention is thoroughly mastered.
Selected jointly as the primary code reference: translates Section 3.2 of the Vaswani paper into minimal, idiomatic PyTorch tensor operations.

source_resources.title: nanoGPT: Simplest, Fastest Repository for Training and Finetuning Medium GPTs
source_resources.author: Andrej Karpathy
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: model.py: CausalSelfAttention forward pass query/key/value projection extraction
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external hyperlink to the public GitHub repository under the permissive MIT license; no proprietary lecture video or transcript text imported.
source_resources.prerequisites: Python, NumPy/PyTorch tensor fundamentals, and feed-forward network basics
source_resources.selection_rationale: Detailed modern reference implementation of clean, idiomatic batched causal self-attention in fewer than 60 lines of code.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Self-contained step-by-step tensor derivations, numeric matrix traces, and pure Python/NumPy implementations are directly provided in curriculum exercises.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Includes extensive production abstraction layers, configuration polymorphism, and cache tracking that obscure direct mathematical tensor operations for beginner learners.
Selected jointly: provides line-by-line literary commentary mapping equations directly to PyTorch tensors.
Expanded video walkthrough; software is MIT-licensed while video audio/subtitles remain linking-only without transcript import.
